---
title: "Untitled"
author: "Levi Winkelman"
date: "2026-01-26"
output: html_document
---

This document contains the code used for harmonizing and visualizing the raw ENU concentration-response data extracted from literature as described in 'Advancing AOPs for genotoxicity through quantifying KERs linking DNA alkylation to increase in mutations and chromosome aberrations' by Winkelman et al., 2026.

```{r,warning=F, message=F}
library(readxl)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(clinPK)
library(ggplot2)
library(mice)
library(lme4)
library(splines)
library(lmerTest)
library(partR2)
library(stats)
source('Functions_data_wrangling.R')
```


-----------
Comet assay
-----------

##General data wrangling##


General first steps in data wrangling
```{r}
#Read in the data
comet = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202603201404_Data_from_literature_search_ENU_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'Comet assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
comet = generalwrangle(comet, conc_col = "Concentration ENU")

#Convert data classess
comet = correctclass(comet)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(comet)
```
Looks good

Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
which(comet$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0)
```
Subtraction from background did not occur.

Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(comet$`Concentration ENU` == 0)
length(unique(comet$`Study index`))
```
Looks good


Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(comet$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```

We have no missing replicates

Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
comet = remove_few_obs_studies(comet)
```


##Check outcome units##

```{r}
table(comet$`Outcome unit (eg % of DNA in tail)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```


##Conversions

Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(comet$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

Convert variability estimates to SDs and SEMs
```{r}
comet = convert_varest(comet)
```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
comet = convert_to_FC(comet, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
table(comet$`Concentration unit (eg μg/ml or μM)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

```{r}
ENU_g_per_mol = 117.11 #Derived from: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Ethylnitrosourea
comet = convert_concs(comet, ENU_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
comet = convert_CTassaytype(comet)
```

Standardize scoring techniques
```{r}
comet = convert_scoringTechnique(comet)
```



##Check for cytotoxicity

We don't have any survival percentage for individual datapoints but survival percentages over the line were stated to be >70%

```{r}
comet$ct = T
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(comet$ct) / nrow(comet)
comet = comet[comet$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
comet = remove_few_obs_studies(comet)
```


##Plot data##

Add extra column for scoring automation
```{r}
#Add a column to map scoring techniques to automated, semi-automated or manual
comet = comet %>%
  mutate(
    `Scoring automation` = case_when(
      `Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` %in% 
        c("manual") ~ "Manual",
      `Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` %in% 
        c("CA4", "Semi-automated (Comet IV)") ~ "Semi-automated",
      `Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` %in% 
        c("Automated (IMSTAR)", "clrmorph", "CeligoS", "Komet6" ) ~ "Automated"
    )
  )
```


Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper
```{r}
comet$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(comet))

#Henderson 1998 paper
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/13.1.89' & comet$`Study index` == 1] = 'repeat 1'
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/13.1.89' & comet$`Study index` == 2] = 'repeat 2'

```


```{r}
doseres_plot(comet, 'all data', assay = 'Comet_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
doseres_contrast(comet, 'Exposure times and enzyme modification', assay = 'Comet_Assay', color_col = 'Time of exposure [h]', shape_col = 'Outcome unit (eg % of DNA in tail)', conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```



#Variance decomposition

```{r}
cometmod = comet
names(cometmod) = make.names(names(cometmod))

cometimp = mice(cometmod, m = 1, method = 'pmm', seed = 20260205)
cometimp = complete(cometimp, 1)
cometimp = prepare_varcomp(cometimp, cometmod)


cometimp2 = cometimp[,c('Author', 'Study.index', 'DOI', 'FC', 'FClog', 'Concentration.ENU', 'Time.of.exposure..h.', 'Outcome.unit..eg...of.DNA.in.tail.', 'Scoring.automation')]
```

```{r}
any(is.na(cometimp2))
```

```{r,message=F,warning=F}
model_comet = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2) +
       Time.of.exposure..h. +
       Outcome.unit..eg...of.DNA.in.tail. +
       Scoring.automation +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = cometimp2
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_comet))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

cometVAR = partR2(model_comet, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2)",
                               "Time.of.exposure..h.",
                               "Outcome.unit..eg...of.DNA.in.tail.",
                               "Scoring.automation"))
cometVAR$R2
cometVAR$model = model_comet
cometVAR$vc = vc
```



------------------
Micronucleus assay
------------------


##General data wrangling##


General first steps in data wrangling
```{r,message=F}
#Read in the data
MN = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202603201404_Data_from_literature_search_ENU_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'Micronucleus assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
MN = generalwrangle(MN, conc_col = "Concentration ENU")

#Convert data classess
MN = correctclass(MN)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(MN)
```
Looks good


Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
MN[which(MN$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0),]
```

We see no subtraction from background


Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(MN$`Concentration ENU` == 0)
length(unique(MN$`Study index`))
```
We have more controls than study indexes, let's see if this is the case because we have raw datapoints

```{r}
any(MN$replicates == 1)
```
Indeed, let's try to summarize the individual measurements

```{r}
MN = ObsToMeans(MN, varOI = 'Study index', ct = T, varextra = NA)
```

Let's check if we still have more controls than datapoints
```{r}
sum(MN$`Concentration ENU` == 0)
length(unique(MN$`Study index`))
```
Looks good


Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(MN$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```
Looks good


Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
MN = remove_few_obs_studies(MN)
```


##Check outcome units##

```{r}
table(MN$`Outcome unit (eg percentage of binucleated cells containing one or more micronuclei)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```
The outcomes can generally be divided into two classes, one for the standard MN assay and one for the CBMN assay, let's standardize the naming and convert promille measurements to percent measurements.
Note that the Bryce study reports Fold changes rather than percentages

```{r}
MN = convert_outcome_units(MN)
```


##Conversions

Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(MN$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

Convert variability estimates to SDs and SEMs
```{r}
MN = convert_varest(MN)
```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
MN = convert_to_FC(MN, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
MN = convert_concs(MN, ENU_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
MN = convert_CTassaytype(MN)
```

Standardize scoring techniques
```{r}
MN = convert_scoringTechnique(MN)
```


##Check for cytotoxicity

```{r}
unique(MN[,c(1:4)][is.na(MN$`Relative survival (%)`),])
```

We have a number studies with missing cytotoxicity measurements,
- The Bryce 2010 studies did not assess cytotox on a case to case basis but reported a viability of over 51% for all concentrations
- Similarly for the Chapman 2014 study, a viability of over 70% has been reported for all concentrations
We will therefore keep all observations in

```{r}
MN$ct[is.na(MN$ct)] = T
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(MN$ct) / nrow(MN)
MN = MN[MN$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
MN = remove_few_obs_studies(MN)
```


#Plotting the data

Optimize variables for plotting and Variance decomposition
```{r}
#Ensure Cytochalasin B variable has two levels only
MN$`Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)` = factor(tolower(MN$`Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)`))
```


Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(MN$Author))
length(unique(MN$`Study index`))
```

Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper
```{r}
MN$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(MN))

#Bryce 2010
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2010.08.020' & MN$`Study index` == 1] = 'repeat 1'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2010.08.020' & MN$`Study index` == 2] = 'repeat 2'

#Cho 2023
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649' & MN$`Study index` == 3] = 'conducted by HC'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649' & MN$`Study index` == 4] = 'conducted by Inotiv-RTP'
```


```{r}
MNplot = MN
names(MNplot)[names(MNplot) == 'Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)'] = 'Scoring technique'
MNplot = MNplot %>%
  mutate(
    `Scoring technique` = recode(
      `Scoring technique`,
      'cellAnalyzer6K' = 'Cell Analyzer 6000',
      'flowCyto' = 'Flow Cytometry'
    )
  )

#Add a column for expression period in days
MN$expression_period = (MN$`Time of harvest [h]` - MN$`Time of exposure [h]`) / 24

#Add a column to map scoring techniques to microscopy based, flow cytometry based or hybrid
MN = MN %>%
  mutate(
    `Scoring technique` = case_when(
      `Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)` %in% 
        c("manual", "semiManualMicroscope", "Metafer", "cellAnalyzer6K") ~ "Microscopy",
      `Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)` %in% 
        c("flowCyto", "Coulter") ~ "Flow Cytometry",
      `Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)` %in% 
        c("imageStream") ~ "Hybrid"
    ), `Assay type` = case_when(
      `Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)` == 'yes' ~ 'CBMN',
      `Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)` == 'no' ~ 'conventional'
    )
  )

```


```{r}
doseres_plot(MN, 'all data', assay = 'MN_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
doseres_contrast(MN, 'Exposure times', assay = 'MN_Assay', color_col = "Time of exposure [h]", conc_col = 'Concentration ENU', shape_col = "Scoring technique", linetype_col = "Assay type", solid_level = 'conventional')
```

##Variance decomposition

```{r}
MNmod = MN
names(MNmod) = make.names(names(MN))

MNimp = mice(MNmod, m = 1, method = 'pmm', seed = 20260205)
MNimp = complete(MNimp, 1)

MNimp2 = prepare_varcomp(MNimp, MNmod)
MNimp2 = MNimp2[,c('Author', 'Study.index', 'DOI', 'FC', 'FClog', 'Concentration.ENU', 'Time.of.exposure..h.', 'expression_period', 'Assay.type', 'Scoring.technique', 'Relative.survival....')]

any(is.na(MNimp2))
```

```{r,message=F,warning=F}
model_MN = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2) +
       Time.of.exposure..h. +
       expression_period +
       Scoring.technique +
       Relative.survival.... +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = MNimp2
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_MN))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

MNVAR = partR2(model_MN, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2)",
                               "Time.of.exposure..h.",
                               "expression_period",
                               "Scoring.technique",
                               "Relative.survival...."
                               ), R2_type = 'marginal'
       )

MNVAR$R2
MNVAR$model = model_MN
MNVAR$vc = vc
```

--------------
Mutation assay
--------------

##General data wrangling##

General first steps in data wrangling
```{r}
#Read in the data
muta = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202603201404_Data_from_literature_search_ENU_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'Forward gene mutation assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
muta = generalwrangle(muta, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU', ctthresh = 10)

#Convert data classess
muta = correctclass(muta)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(muta)
```
Looks good


Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
muta[which(muta$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0),]
```
We see no subtraction from background


Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(muta$`Concentration ENU` == 0)
length(unique(muta$`Study index`))
```
Looks good


Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(muta$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```
We have no missing replicates


Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
muta = remove_few_obs_studies(muta)
```


##Check outcome units##
```{r}
table(muta$`Outcome unit (eg Mutation frequency in percentage)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

Standardize the outcome
```{r}
muta = convert_muta_to_perm(muta)
```


##Conversions

Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(muta$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

Convert variability estimates to SDs and SEMs
```{r}
muta = convert_varest(muta)
```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
muta = convert_to_FC(muta, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
muta = convert_concs(muta, ENU_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
muta = convert_CTassaytype(muta)
```

Standardize locus naming
```{r}
muta = convert_locus_naming(muta)
```


##Check for cytotoxicity

```{r}
table(muta$`Relative survival (%)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

See where there is cytotoxicity data missing
```{r}
muta[,c(2:4)][is.na(muta$`Relative survival (%)`),]
```


The only missing datapoint for relative survival is the 100 uM concentration, since the reported survival is still reported to be ~50 for a higher concentration, we will mark this observation as non cytotoxic

```{r}
muta$ct = muta$`Relative survival (%)` >= 20 | is.na(muta$`Relative survival (%)`)
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(muta$ct) / nrow(muta)
muta = muta[muta$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
muta = remove_few_obs_studies(muta)
```
 

#Plotting the data

Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(muta$Author))
length(unique(muta$`Study index`))
```
Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper
```{r}
muta$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(muta))

#Jensen 1986 paper
muta$distinct[muta$DOI == '10.1016/0027-5107(86)90033-3' & muta$`Gene locus` == 'TK'] = 'TK locus'
muta$distinct[muta$DOI == '10.1016/0027-5107(86)90033-3' & muta$`Gene locus` == 'HPRT'] = 'HPRT locus'

```


```{r}
doseres_plot(muta, 'all data', assay = 'mutation_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```

This all looks nice and comparable

#Variance decomposition

```{r}
mutamod = muta
names(mutamod) = make.names(names(mutamod))

mutamod = prepare_varcomp(mutamod)

mutamod = mutamod[,c("Study.index", "Author", "DOI", "Gene.locus", "Concentration.ENU", "Relative.survival....", "FC", "FClog")]
```

No imputation is needed because we have no missing data for any of the columns of interest

```{r,message=F,warning=F}
model_muta = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2) +
       Gene.locus +
       Relative.survival.... +
       (1|Study.index),
  data = mutamod
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_muta))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

mutaVAR = partR2(model_muta, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2)",
                               "Gene.locus",
                               "Relative.survival...."
                               ), R2_type = 'marginal')

mutaVAR$R2
mutaVAR$model = model_muta
mutaVAR$vc = vc
```

Chromosome aberration assay

##General data wrangling##

General first steps in data wrangling
```{r}
#Read in the data
CAA = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202603201404_Data_from_literature_search_ENU_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'Chromosome aberration assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
CAA = generalwrangle(CAA, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')

#Convert data classess
CAA = correctclass(CAA)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(CAA)
```
Looks good

Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
CAA[which(CAA$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0),]
```
Looks good

Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(CAA$`Concentration ENU` == 0)
length(unique(CAA$`Study index`))
```
The Greenwood studies don't have a control and will be removed in a later step for having too few observations


Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(CAA$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```
We have no missing replicates

Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
CAA = remove_few_obs_studies(CAA)
```


##Check outcome units##
```{r}
table(CAA$`Outcome unit (eg aberrations per cell)`)
```
All looks good, no need for conversions


##Conversions

Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(CAA$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```
Convert variability estimates to SDs and SEMs
```{r}
CAA = convert_varest(CAA)
```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
CAA = convert_to_FC(CAA, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
CAA = convert_concs(CAA, ENU_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
CAA = convert_CTassaytype(CAA)
```

Standardize scoring techniques
```{r}
CAA = convert_scoringTechnique(CAA)
```

##Check for cytotoxicity

Due to scarcity of our data, we decided to keep a somewhat liberal survival threshold of 20%

```{r}
CAA$ct = CAA$`Relative survival (%)` >= 20
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(CAA$ct) / nrow(CAA)
CAA = CAA[CAA$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
CAA = remove_few_obs_studies(CAA)
```

#Plotting the data

Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(CAA$Author))
length(unique(CAA$`Study index`))
```
We only have one study after data wrangling



```{r,warning=F}
doseres_plot(CAA, 'all data', assay = 'CAA_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')
```

#Variance decomposition

Since we only have one study for the CAA on ENU, we cannot perform a Variance decomposition but we can check out the r squared of the simplest linear model
```{r}
CAAmod = CAA
names(CAAmod) = make.names(names(CAAmod)) 
CAAmod = CAAmod[,c("Study.index", "Author", "DOI", "Concentration.ENU", "Time.of.harvest..h.", "FC", "ct")]
```

No imputation is needed because we have no missing data for any of the columns of interest

```{r}
model_CAA = lm(
  FC ~ poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2),
  data = CAAmod
)
```


```{r}
summary(model_CAA)$r.squared
```

##Plotting the data

Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(ECDS$Author))
length(unique(ECDS$`Study index`))
```

Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper
```{r}
ECDS$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(ECDS))

ECDS$expression_period = (ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` - ECDS$`Time of exposure [h]`) / 24

#Cho 2023 paper
ECDS$distinct[ECDS$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649'& ECDS$Comments == 'Performed by Health Canada (HC)' & ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` == 48] = 'conducted by HC, 48h harvest'
ECDS$distinct[ECDS$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649'& ECDS$Comments == 'Performed by Health Canada (HC)' & ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` == 72] = 'conducted by HC, 72h harvest'
ECDS$distinct[ECDS$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649'& ECDS$Comments == 'Performed by Health Canada (HC)' & ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` == 96] = 'conducted by HC, 96h harvest'
ECDS$distinct[ECDS$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649'& ECDS$Comments == 'Performed by Inotiv-RTP' & ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` == 48] = 'conducted by Inotiv-RTP, 48h harvest'
ECDS$distinct[ECDS$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649'& ECDS$Comments == 'Performed by Inotiv-RTP' & ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` == 72] = 'conducted by Inotiv-RTP, 72h harvest'
ECDS$distinct[ECDS$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2023.503649'& ECDS$Comments == 'Performed by Inotiv-RTP' & ECDS$`Time of harvest [h]` == 96] = 'conducted by Inotiv-RTP, 96h harvest'
```

```{r}
doseres_plot(ECDS, 'all data', assay = 'ECDS_Assay', width = 12, conc_col = 'Concentration ENU')

doseres_contrast(ECDS, "Harvest times and sequencing techniques", assay = 'ECDS_Assay', color_col = "Time of harvest [h]", shape_col = "Technique for scoring", conc_col = 'Concentration ENU', save = T, path = '../Figures/ConcRes_comparison/FigS1')
```

```{r}
ECDSmod = ECDS
names(ECDSmod) = make.names(names(ECDSmod))

ECDSmod = prepare_varcomp(ECDSmod)

ECDSmod = ECDSmod[,c('Study.index', 'Author', 'DOI', 'Concentration.ENU', 'Target.region', 'expression_period', 'Relative.survival....', 'Technique.for.scoring', 'FC', 'FClog')]
```

No need for imputation since we have data on all our explanatory variables of interest

```{r,message=F,warning=F}
model_ECDS = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2) +
       Target.region +
       expression_period  +
       Relative.survival.... +
       Technique.for.scoring +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = ECDSmod
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_ECDS))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

ECDSVAR = partR2(model_ECDS, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.ENU, degree = 2)",
                               "Target.region",
                               "expression_period",
                               "Relative.survival....",
                               "Technique.for.scoring"
                               ), R2_type = 'marginal')

ECDSVAR$R2
ECDSVAR$model = model_ECDS
ECDSVAR$vc = vc
```
